root_causes.description: The frontend pod was abruptly terminated and immediately replaced: Kubernetes emitted a 'Killing: Stopping container frontend' event followed by scheduling, creation and start of a new pod (frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8). CPU and memory were normal and no application error logs were produced, indicating abrupt container termination (crash/restart) rather than an application-level or downstream dependency fault.

evidence.observed_value: Killing: Stopping container frontend (count=1) during 08:14:49-08:21:49 window
evidence.expected_baseline: no container kill events for a healthy steady-state pod
no pod recreation in steady state

evidence.observed_value: mean=148.19, p50=8.01, p95=432.87, max=604.82 with anomaly flagged (request throughput collapse/spike consistent with pod downtime then recovery)
evidence.expected_baseline: stable frontend request rate at steady load, no collapse/spike

evidence.observed_value: max=0.000 (restart counter reset because a new pod object replaced the killed one)
no logs found - no application-level error/panic, consistent with abrupt external pod termination
evidence.expected_baseline: in-process faults would surface application errors

root_causes.description: Lower-probability alternative: the termination could have been triggered by memory pressure/OOM. Observed working-set memory stayed within normal range, so this is not supported.

evidence.expected_baseline: frontend working set ~250 MB; OOM would show limit saturation

root_causes.description: Lowest-probability alternative: frontend could be disrupted by a downstream dependency. Downstream error rates were low and no dependency error spike was observed, so this is unlikely.

remediation_steps: Inspect the previous frontend container: kubectl describe pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 and kubectl logs --previous to capture the termination reason and exit code.
Check the frontend Deployment for restart-cause indicators (OOMKilled, liveness probe failure, node eviction) and verify replicas stayed at desired count during the kill.
Ensure multiple frontend replicas, a PodDisruptionBudget, and anti-affinity spread so a single pod kill does not impact availability.
Add/adjust liveness and readiness probes, and if the exit was OOMKilled raise the container memory limit; otherwise investigate node-level or platform-initiated evictions.
Add alerting on kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and container kill events for the frontend to catch future crashes earlier.
